title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity, from international collaborations on asteroid missions to significant defense contracts. Meanwhile, budget allocations and technological advancements continue to shape the landscape.

themes.title: International Collaborations Flourish
themes.body: ESA and JAXA's finalized agreement on the Apophis mission underscores the growing trend of cross-border partnerships in space exploration. Paraguay's signing of the Artemis Accords further illustrates the expanding global commitment to lunar endeavors.

themes.title: Defense Contracts on the Rise
themes.body: Viasat's $307 million contract with the Marine Corps highlights the increasing demand for satellite communications in defense operations. Additionally, Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program signals continued investment in ground station capabilities.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's $1.4 billion addition to the space resilience line indicates a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. This funding could enhance the U.S. position in an increasingly contested orbital environment.

themes.title: Technological Developments Persist
themes.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant has cleared a critical design review, marking a step forward in reusable spacecraft technology. Meanwhile, MDA Space's ongoing work on the Gateway robotic arm continues to pave the way for lunar infrastructure.
